subject: Business
title: How Tax Brackets Actually Work
description: A quick, practical guide to How Tax Brackets Actually Work.

hook.text: Someone says 'If I earn more, I'll move to a higher bracket and take home less.' That's not how it works.

buildup.text: Tax brackets are marginal: each bracket only applies to income within that range, not your total income.

discovery.text: If the 22% bracket starts at $44K, only dollars above $44K are taxed at 22%. Everything below is taxed at lower rates.

twist.text: Your 'effective' tax rate is always lower than your top marginal rate. Most people pay far less than they think.

climax.text: Earning $1 more never results in taking home less. The marginal system ensures every additional dollar is net positive.

punchline.text: You're never punished for earning more. Each dollar is taxed on its own.

quiz.question: How do marginal tax brackets work?
options: Only income within each bracket is taxed at that bracket's rate
Your entire income is taxed at your highest bracket rate
Higher earners pay the same rate as lower earners

details.summary: Tax brackets are marginal, meaning only income within each bracket is taxed at that rate, not your entire income. Moving into a higher bracket does not retroactively increase taxes on lower earnings, a common misconception that discourages people from earning more.
details.whyItMatters: The marginal tax misconception leads people to turn down raises or bonuses fearing they will lose money to taxes. Understanding that only additional income is taxed at the higher rate eliminates this irrational fear.
takeaways: Only income within each bracket is taxed at that bracket's rate
Your effective tax rate is always lower than your highest marginal rate
Earning more always leaves you with more after-tax income

faq.question: Can you actually lose money by moving into a higher tax bracket?
faq.answer: No. Because brackets are marginal, only the dollars above the threshold are taxed at the higher rate. A raise that pushes you into the next bracket only increases taxes on the amount exceeding that threshold. You always keep more money after earning more.

faq.question: What is the difference between marginal and effective tax rates?
faq.answer: Your marginal rate is the tax on your last dollar of income. Your effective rate is total taxes paid divided by total income. If you earn 60,000 dollars, your marginal rate might be 22 percent, but your effective rate will be lower because the first portions were taxed at lower rates.
